summary: The Securing Enhanced Programs, Systems, and Initiatives for Sepsis Act (SEPSIS Act) establishes federal programs directed by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to reduce the rates, complications, and fatalities of sepsis. The bill authorizes $20 million annually from fiscal years 2026 through 2030 to support educational campaigns, improve data collection, coordinate healthcare agency efforts, and create a hospital recognition program.

affected_groups.effect: May participate in voluntary recognition programs, report sepsis program data using assessment tools, and adopt CDC sepsis best practices.
Potentially benefit from improved hospital data tracking, better early recognition protocols, and reduced rates of sepsis complications and readmissions.

key_provisions: Establishes a dedicated sepsis team at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to lead education campaigns on hospital best practices, improve pediatric sepsis data collection, and share information with the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services.

Requires the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to submit a report within one year to congressional committees regarding the development and implementation of adult and pediatric sepsis outcome measures.
Mandates annual briefings to congressional committees on hospital adoption of sepsis best practices, pediatric sepsis rates, inter-agency coordination, and quality of care evaluations.
Authorizes the Secretary to establish a voluntary honor roll program to recognize hospitals that maintain or improve effective sepsis programs based on public benchmarks.
Authorizes appropriations of $20,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030 to carry out these sepsis programs.
missing_information: Specific criteria for the hospital honor roll selection benchmarks are not detailed in the text.
Details on how the authorized funds will be precisely divided among the various administrative tasks are not specified.
